newsitem.title: GREECE: Cyprus United Stockbrokers opens branch in Athens.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus United Stockbrokers opens branch in Athens.

text.p: Cyprus stock exchange member United Stockbrokers is the first Cypriot brokerage to establish a presence in Greece with a representative office in Athens, aiming to attract Greek investors to Cyprus' equity market.
United Stockbrokers offices at Dragatsaniou 8 are located in the financial district very close to Sophocleous street, home of the Athens bourse.

"The office will assist investors interested in Cyprus' equities market and provide advice on listing requirements and the advantages of Cyprus as an off-shore centre," United Stockbrokers managing director Adonis Yiagou told Reuters.
The securities firm offers eligible Cypriot investors on-line price information on the Athens bourse and a wide range of Greek investment vehicles.
Listed investment companies and insurance firms are currently allowed to invest up to 20 percent of their assets in Greece under Cyprus law.
"Foreign exchange controls will be lifted soon -- we hope within 1997 -- and Cypriots will be allowed to invest in Greece," Yagou said.
This, he said, was expected to generate significant flows towards the Greek markets once controls were lifted.

"It's natural to expect a pick-up in investment flows since the two countries share the same language, there is easy access to information and there are Cypriot banks already present in Greece," he said.

The Cyprus stock exchange is working towards full computerisation of trading and settlement and expects completion by the summer of 1998. This will be coupled with share dematerialisation -- paperless settlement.

As a result brokers will see their back office costs reduced. Additionally, the deregulation of brokers' commissions which is expected to take place during the same period will lower breakevens and contribute to higher trading volumes.
Capital gains from trading in shares are not taxed and there is full repatriation of capital and profits.
